Reference / encoding/utf

encoding/utf#

Explicit, immutable UTF codecs.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let network is @byte = Utf16Encoded(
    origin: "A😀",
    order: ByteOrder.big,
).bytes();
// [0, 65, 216, 61, 222, 0]

let restored is string = Utf16Decoded(
    origin: network,
    order: ByteOrder.big,
).string();

Description#

Explicit, immutable UTF codecs.

UTF-8 has one canonical byte order. UTF-16 and UTF-32 always require an explicit ByteOrder: serialized APIs never inherit a machine-native order. Encoders do not add a BOM. Decoders do not detect, strip or use a BOM to change order; U+FEFF is decoded as an ordinary scalar value.

InvalidUtf8, InvalidUtf16 and InvalidUtf32 report the byte offset at which the first malformed scalar begins. An incomplete final code unit starts at its first trailing byte. Decoders reject overlong UTF-8, surrogate scalars, unpaired UTF-16 surrogates and values above U+10FFFF. No codec normalizes text or inserts replacement characters.
